verdict: Malicious skimmer that harvests payment credentials and exfiltrates them to an external server
summary: The script enumerates common credit‑card input fields, captures their values (including passwords, email, cookies, and page URL), and continuously exfiltrates the data via navigator.sendBeacon or an image pixel. It uses a base64‑obfuscated endpoint (api.cdn-metrics-cloud.top) and runs heartbeat checks, indicating a classic Magecart form‑jacking payload.

text: Collects values from credit‑card related input fields, email fields, cookies, and the current URL
Triggers exfiltration on every keyup, change, submit, and periodic heartbeat
Encodes collected data as Base64 JSON and sends it to a remote endpoint using navigator.sendBeacon with an image fallback

data: credit‑card number, expiry, CVV/CVC, security code, cardholder name, password, email, document.cookie, location.href
same payload via Image GET request (fallback)

title: Form‑jacking skimmer harvesting payment credentials
evidence: var CARD_SELECTORS = [ 'input[name="cc-number"]', ... 'input[type="password"]' ]; ... store[el.name || el.getAttribute("autocomplete") || sel] = el.value;
impact: Attackers can obtain full payment card data and passwords, enabling fraudulent transactions and PCI DSS violations
recommendation: Immediately remove the script from all pages, especially payment pages, and block its source domain

title: Unauthorized exfiltration of sensitive data to external domain
impact: Personal and payment data are transmitted outside the merchant’s control, breaching PCI DSS 6.4.3 and GDPR/CCPA consent requirements
recommendation: Block outbound connections to the decoded endpoint and enforce CSP restrictions

title: Access to document.cookie without user consent
impact: Cookies may contain session identifiers or tracking data that can be abused for session hijacking
recommendation: Avoid reading cookies in client‑side scripts unless strictly necessary and ensure they are HttpOnly where appropriate

title: Base64 obfuscation of endpoint URL
impact: Obfuscation makes analysis harder but does not add functional security; it is a typical evasion technique
recommendation: Decode and monitor such URLs; consider static analysis rules for atob usage

pci: Violates PCI DSS 6.4.3 (secure coding) and 11.6.1 (monitoring) – script exfiltrates card data to an unauthorised third‑party, making the payment page unsafe
privacy: Collects personal data (email, cookies, URL) and payment credentials without explicit consent, breaching GDPR and CCPA requirements

text: Delete the malicious script from all pages; replace with a vetted, PCI‑compliant payment integration
If the script must remain for legacy reasons, load it in a sandboxed iframe with CSP restricting connect-src to trusted domains only
Add a strict Content Security Policy that blocks script-src from cdn.example.com and connect-src to only the merchant’s own API endpoints

policy: script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.cdn-metrics-cloud.top; img-src 'self' https://api.cdn-metrics-cloud.top; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self';
notes: Only allow connections to trusted merchant domains; the external endpoint should be blocked unless explicitly required for legitimate analytics

note: Random session identifier included in every payload
